newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses scale peaks, boosted by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses scale peaks, boosted by Wall St.

text.p: Major European bourses scaled new peaks on Friday after a wave of investor confidence drove Wall Street to an all-time high while the dollar hit a four-year high against the yen.
London, Frankfurt and Paris raced to trading records on the strength of New York's overnight performance, which cracked the 7,000-point barrier on the Dow Jones average for the first time.
On currency markets, the dollar approached the psychologically important level of 125 yen before falling back as traders were hit by jitters over fears of central bank moves to curb its rise.

Europe's biggest stock market, London, climbed 0.5 percent to 4,349.0 points on the FTSE index with investors encouraged by New York's performance, bid activity and strong debt markets. The previous high was set on February 10.
But it was the Dow's strength, fuelled by low interest rates and non-inflationary economic growth, that injected new life into the bull run on the big European stock markets.

The Dow ended up 60.81 points at an all-time high of 7,022.44, beating the previous record set just Wednesday. The rally capped a breathtaking run that has added 1,000 points to the blue-chip index in just four months.

"Wall Street has done particularly well because corporate America has done particularly well," said Mark Tinker, UK equity strategist at UBS. "UK corporations are doing well, but the UK market is just following."
He added that British equities have been a bit more restrained by the upcoming general election, which must be held by May."I wouldn't chase the market with the FTSE 100 over 4,300," he said.
A recommended cash offer from Williams Holdings Plc of 1.3 billion sterling ($2.1 billion) for Chubb Security Plc also buoyed sentiment.
European bourses are seeing record-breaking runs as low inflation has reduced interest rate pressure and the strong dollar enhances prospects for exporting businesses.

But markets will be keeping a wary eye open for clues on the health of the influential U.S. economy contained in wholesale inflation data for January and business inventories for December due at 1330 GMT.
In Frankfurt, shares climbed 0.9 percent on the GDAX index, registering a trading high of 3,260.94 points before easing slightly, supported by Wall Street and the stronger dollar.
But some dealers fretted that a correction in the markets was due and that buying was slackening off. "You get the feeling a lot of funds are already fully invested," said one dealer.
In Paris, shares climbed to an intra-day high of 2,643.98 on the CAC-40 index, building on Thursday's rise of more than one percent. But stocks slipped in later trading.
Traders said the Dow's push, benign bond markets and a strong dollar were all fuelling the CAC's ascent to record highs.

On foreign exchanges, as the dollar headed for 125 yen, analysts said the higher the U.S. currency goes, the more the market fears the possibility that central banks, principally the Bank of Japan, will move in to halt its rise.
The U.S. currency ran out of steam at 124.82 yen and fell below 1.69 marks but still looked capable of an assault on 125 and 1.70 on the basis of strong U.S. fundamentals, analysts said.

"I think that it (125) is going to be a very difficult psychological level to get through," said Adrian Davies, senior strategist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull here. "There are rumours that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will intervene at 125."
"The market is going to carry on buying dollars until you see action rather than empty words from the G7," said Nick Parsons, forex strategist at Banque Paribas in London.
The dollar has been drawing support from the buoyant U.S. asset markets and there is plenty of U.S. data for the market to feed off on Friday, with the main offering January producer prices.
CURRENCIES AT 1245 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6848 marks and 124.06 yen compared with 1.6877 marks and 124.44 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1245 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 22.7 points at 4,349.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 1.15 points at 2,629.56.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 18.7 points at 3,248.18.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $342.50 an ounce, compared with Thursday's close of $341.85. Silver was at $5.14, up two cents.
